title: Chapter 1089
paragraphs: Chapter 1089
Episode 255. The Death of Kelliark Zipple, and....(6)
Kelliark Zipple and Malugia continued their fierce battle in the Empire for about a week even after the Vamel Alliance had retreated.
No one witnessed that battle directly. Because not even the Vamel Alliance had redeployed troops to the fierce battleground.

It was because, even by the standards of the Genesis Knights, it was an overly dangerous battle. For the coalition, the most rational choice was to wait for the two horrific beings to destroy each other, or for one side to suffer serious damage and the war to end.
The fight between Kelliark and Malugia suddenly ended this morning.

The result of the fight was unknown. It had ended so suddenly that not even the Genesis Knights, who had been on standby in the Empire's territorial waters to ambush the victor, could grasp the situation.
All that remained were the traces of the great nation called the Empire, which had become a golden wasteland.
The Empire had fallen.

More than seventy percent of its territory had been swept away and destroyed by the aftereffects of the battle, and even more of its people had died. In the areas that had been affected by the power of the two beings, even for a moment, even a little, no survivors or any debris remained.
Therefore, the scenery was completely different from a case where a place was ruined due to a normal war. Just an endless stretch of a golden wasteland, symbolizing Malugia's power.
No cries of grief, no pleas to be saved, no voices seeking God, not even a single stone from a broken building could be seen.
Before that overwhelmingly desolate landscape, Jin and his companions stood with dazed faces.
“The records... I have to analyze the records... Valeria.”
The whereabouts of Kelliark and Malugia.
They had to know where those monsters had gone. To get revenge for this world.
“Although we can't know why they suddenly stopped fighting, neither of them can be in a normal state. We must finish them off before they recover.”
Vahn said, gritting her teeth.
Be it Kelliark or Malugia, the fact that they each single-handedly surpassed the entire military strength of the coalition had already been revealed.
When they were in their complete state, it was impossible to win no matter what they did. Any formidable enemy they had faced so far seemed shabby in comparison to them.
Tears fell from Valeria's two eyes as she analyzed the records. A death that could not be fathomed or felt was madly updating the record screen.
“Perhaps they didn't end the fight, but just moved the battlefield to another dimension.”
Jin nodded at Murakan's words. The great dimensional gate that Malugia had opened by taking Focal's power was now gone.
“Even if we can't find them, they will surely reveal themselves. Since the goal of both is to either conquer or destroy this world.”
Which one would reveal themselves first, which one would they be able to track first.
Jin somehow had an intuition that it would be Kelliark's side. If he hadn't died, he would now appear, leading his army.
'Even if Kelliark received a massive blow in his battle with Malugia, if the Demon Army is added... how on earth are we supposed to stand against them?'
To finish turning the Battle God Temple's main hall into a flying fortress, and for Chiron's expedition to return.
For now, those were the only two ways to strengthen the coalition's forces. However, he could not think that either of those two elements would be superior to the Demon Army.
'Solderet's arrangement...'
Solderet's final arrangement in the Black Sea.
A chance of victory would only emerge if there was something inside it that could turn this situation around.
'And the Witch. I have to make her participate in the war directly. Even if there is some restriction that makes her use Orgal instead, I have to get rid of that restriction somehow.'
The moment he thought that far, a steel dimensional gate opened and Orgal revealed himself.
Unlike usual, he was not acting like a madman, nor did he have a face full of mischief.
He too was grieving. At the fact that the Empire had fallen, at the fact that this world had already been destroyed this much.
And he was feeling sorry. Because he had not been of much help in this battle.
[Jin, I am sorry.]
“If you hadn't appeared even then, more people would have died during the retreat. Cut the useless talk. More importantly, I need to meet the Witch.”
[...Helluram?]
“You know better than anyone. That there is no answer unless she stands on our side and fights directly.”

[I will relay the message to Helluram for now. But it's best not to have high hopes. I too have requested her support in numerous worlds... Above all, even if she does step up directly, that would be no different from the birth of a lesser evil.]

-[Alright! Alright, alright. Then let's sort this out, Helluram. So to speak, I was your lover, that is, your contractor. In who knows how many identical worlds, Orgal Remillias was always your contractor. But I always fail. At what? From my perspective, it's the resurrection of Kinzelo, and from your perspective, what is it? What do you want, really? As far as I know, it's for the light to disappear from the world. That's why we broke up.]
-[Yes, that is still a valid story.]
Orgal recalled his past conversation with Helluram and gave a bitter smile. To erase 'light' from the world, that too, in the end, was nothing more than another apocalypse.
“Still, a lesser evil is better than the worst evil.”
[I see what you mean. By the way, Dante Hairan just woke up.]
“...Dante did?”
Dante Hairan, he had been unconscious ever since he was dramatically rescued in the last battle. It was because the accumulated shock was too great.
However, a bigger problem than the physical damage was his mind. He had felt a moment of salvation seeing his friends right before he collapsed, but he had intuited an even darker future.
The intuition that the Empire might end as it was, that had, in the end, become fact.
[If Ainas hadn't directly entered Dante's dream, they say they wouldn't have known when he would have woken up. He still does not know what happened to the Empire.]
Squeeze, Jin closed his eyes for a moment.
“...I will meet him and tell him.”
Soon, Jin headed for Kinzelo's hideout through Orgal's steel dimensional gate.
Even Bubar and Ainas were not joking around like usual. When he reached the medical room where Dante was, he could see him and Veradin.
“Jin.”
“Dante.”
“The Empire... has it fallen?”
A long silence followed. Now that he was in front of Dante, Jin felt as if his mouth were frozen shut.
“...Grandfather. The Sword Emperor's Holy Land, has that light that my grandfather left behind also disappeared?”
“The Sword Emperor's Holy Land is safe... Dante.”
Only the Sword Emperor's Holy Land is safe.

He couldn't bring himself to say it like that. He couldn't bring himself to inform him that only the Sword Emperor's Holy Land had, strangely, received no particular damage, and that all the other major cities and feudal states were finished, that only some of the small cities on the various borders were safe.
However, Dante could tell. Tears of blood flowed from his empty eyes.
“Jin. Can we... even win? Against those horrific beings, can we truly get our revenge?”
Guilt boiled up every time he heard each of Dante's words. Why on earth had he regressed, why was he in charge of the task that Orgal had failed at in those numerous worlds.
He hadn't known from the beginning, but now, the path ahead was even more hazy.
Nevertheless, Jin heavily nodded his head.
“We have to. We must.”
Dante rose from his seat and wiped away his tears of blood. His fist and cheek were stained red.

“I will honor the resentful spirits of my dead people after our revenge is complete. So do not prepare a separate memorial service at the coalition level. I... would like to be alone for a moment. I will collect myself for a moment, and then return to the front lines immediately.”
Dante left the medical room. Jin watched his retreating back, then met Veradin's eyes.
“Jin, I debated whether or not to tell you this. But I think it's better to.”
“What is it?”
“When Lady Silkia and Orgal formed the dimensional gate for the retreat, I was unconscious. You remember, right?”
“You were.”
“At that time, I had a dream. I'm confused about whether it was a dream or not... but anyway, I think I heard Lady Elona's voice at that time.”
“What did you say?”

“It's hard to explain, but from the moment Malugia appeared and throughout the battle, I felt as if Lady Elona within her was conscious of me. In reality, Malugia never once attacked me directly. I don't know if it was because she didn't have the room to, or if I wasn't worth it.”
“You believe that Lady Elona's consciousness still remains within Malugia, Veradin.”

“...Yes. It could just be my wish, and it could be a vain hope... but for some reason, the voice I heard in my dream that day has been getting clearer as the days go by. And only today did I remember its contents completely, and I concluded that it would be best to tell you.”
“What were the contents?”
“When Malugia kills Kelliark, I will create an opportunity for you to kill Malugia. And, when you face Kelliark and the Demon Army, use Octavia Zipple.”
Jin's eyes widened.

“...The first part is something Lady Elona would naturally say if her consciousness is alive. It would be great if Lady Elona really does remain within that monster. But, what's this about Octavia Zipple all of a sudden?”

“According to the story Lady Elona told me in my dream that day, the leader of the Demon Army, that Kelliark Zipple, has an oddly human-like emotion remaining only for my aunt. I don't know if it's pity, curiosity, or interest. She didn't explain in detail; it seemed like she was trying to avoid Malugia's eyes.”
Octavia Zipple, her whereabouts were currently unknown. At least, until this dimension's Kelliark died and the leader of the Demon Army appeared, there had been no news of her being killed in action.
“It's a bit out of the blue, but now is the time when we have to rely on anything we can get. I'll tell Valeria and Lord Leuth to try and analyze the records on Octavia.”
